title: The Nature of Epistemology and Skepticism
text:
Epistemology is the branch of philosophy concerned with knowledge itself—its nature, scope, and validity. It attempts to answer fundamental questions such as: what is knowledge, and how do we acquire it? Core debates often revolve around whether genuine knowledge requires empirical evidence (a priori knowledge) or if rational deduction alone is sufficient.

Skepticism represents one of the most significant challenges to epistemology. Radical skepticism questions the possibility of certain knowledge, suggesting that all claims about reality might be unfounded due to potential cognitive biases or sensory illusions. Historically, thinkers have developed various frameworks, such as coherentism and foundationalism, to argue for specific sources of justified belief.

The relationship between experience (empiricism) and innate ideas (rationalism) remains a defining tension within the field. Philosophy continues to refine methods for determining what constitutes justifiable belief, moving beyond mere opinion toward reasoned certainty.
